components.css: .ds-project-card { display:flex; min-height:420px; flex-direction:column; padding:21px; border:1px solid rgba(21,42,64,.08); border-radius:18px; background:#f6efc9; box-shadow:0 16px 34px rgba(47,62,82,.09); color:#152a40; font-family:'DM Sans',Arial,sans-serif; text-decoration:none; transition:transform .28s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),box-shadow .28s ease; } .ds-project-card:hover { box-shadow:0 26px 45px rgba(47,62,82,.15); transform:translateY(-6px); } .ds-project-card:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #263cce; outline-offset:4px; } .ds-meta { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; font-size:11px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.02em; } .ds-meta span { color:#556478; font-weight:600; } .ds-window { position:relative; width:80%; height:152px; margin:auto; border:1px solid rgba(21,42,64,.19); border-radius:12px; background:rgba(255,255,255,.52); box-shadow:12px 15px 0 rgba(21,42,64,.08); transform:rotate(-4deg); transition:transform .35s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); } .ds-project-card:hover .ds-window { transform:rotate(-1deg) translateY(-5px); } .ds-window i,.ds-window b,.ds-window em { position:absolute; display:block; border-radius:5px; background:rgba(21,42,64,.16); } .ds-window i { top:16px; left:16px; width:45%; height:8px; } .ds-window b { top:42px; left:16px; width:18%; height:92px; } .ds-window em { top:42px; right:16px; width:55%; height:64px; } .ds-copy h3 { margin:0 0 9px; font-family:'Instrument Serif',Georgia,serif; font-size:42px; font-weight:400; letter-spacing:-.035em; line-height:.95; } .ds-copy p { margin:0 0 15px; color:#556478; font-size:13px; line-height:1.45; } .ds-tag { display:inline-block; padding:5px 8px; border:1px solid rgba(21,42,64,.16); border-radius:999px; font-size:10px; font-weight:600; }

components.html:
Hello, I’m Karishma.

A concise tile holds one thought with room for it to land.
components.css: .ds-tile { display:flex; min-height:300px; flex-direction:column; justify-content:flex-end; padding:clamp(24px,3vw,44px); border-radius:18px; background:#fcfbf8; color:#152a40; font-family:'DM Sans',Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-kicker { margin:0 0 18px; color:#263cce; font-size:15px; font-weight:700; } .ds-tile h2 { max-width:10ch; margin:0 0 22px; font-family:'Instrument Serif',Georgia,serif; font-size:clamp(3rem,8vw,5.5rem); font-weight:400; letter-spacing:-.04em; line-height:.87; } .ds-body { max-width:44ch; margin:0; color:#556478; font-size:16px; line-height:1.55; }

narrative.overview:
This is a personal editorial portfolio in Experience mode: the work takes the foreground, while navigation and controls recede into a calm, precise frame. Warm paper gives the page a tactile, considered base; deep navy provides the seriousness needed for complex enterprise and AI work; a rotating family of powder blue, pale butter, and muted lilac tiles gives each story room to breathe.

The system behaves like an arranged worktable rather than a conventional stacked website. Generous bento tiles create a paced sequence of introduction, proof, project work, perspective, experience, and contact. Expressive serif headlines carry the human point of view; compact sans-serif UI copy keeps the experience practical and legible. Case-study routes inherit this world so the homepage reads as the front door, not a visual detour.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial, personal, and quietly confident rather than promotional.
Warm light surfaces with deep-navy contrast and one restrained cobalt signal.
Varied rounded bento tiles that make the portfolio feel composed, not templated.
Large, close-set serif statements paired with compact, clear sans-serif information.
Minimal motion: small hover lifts and deliberate scroll behavior, never ambient spectacle.

rules.name: The Color-Field Rule
rules.body: Use a single pastel field per tile and let paper or ink create the counterpoint. Do not combine multiple pastels inside one card.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Use Instrument Serif for authored statements and project titles; use DM Sans for everything visitors need to scan, compare, or operate.

rules.name: The Varied-Grid Rule
rules.body: Keep tile proportions intentionally uneven within a section, then use the shared gap and rounded edges to make the composition feel like one system.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Tiles stay flat at rest. Reserve lifted depth for interactive case-study cards and primary actions.

dos: Do lead major statements and project titles with Instrument Serif, then use DM Sans for the supporting information around them.
Do create hierarchy through varied tile proportions, paper space, and tonal fields before adding borders or effects.
Do give each project or editorial idea one clear pastel or paper tile field.
Do preserve the shared bento corner language and repeated interior gap when extending into case-study routes.
Do respect reduced-motion preferences by removing transitions and smooth scrolling.
donts: Don't turn the portfolio into a dense dashboard, marketing funnel, or uniform card gallery.
Don't use more than one pastel field within a single bento tile or project card.
Don't add heavy shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, or decorative motion that competes with the work.
Don't use Instrument Serif for dense metadata, navigation, tags, or long explanatory paragraphs.
Don't make hover movement necessary to understand or access content.
